analysis.title: SpaceX: Compute-driven state of mind
key_insights: DB previews SpaceX 3Q26 earnings, due tomorrow after market close, one day before Tesla reports. It expects in-line results with potential upside in profitability. Reiterates Buy and $235 price target.

3Q26 model: revenue $12.6bn (+127% YoY), gross margin about 59%, adjusted EBITDA above $6.6bn. The AI segment gets a full quarter of cloud hosting revenue, rising almost 3x sequentially to about $6bn.
Connectivity is modeled at nearly $5bn of revenue (+60% YoY), with consumer broadband subscribers at 13.5m (vs 12.0m in 2Q26) and ARPU down $2 QoQ to $64.
3Q26 capex is forecast at $19bn, mainly for AI compute, lifting capacity to 1.8 GW and producing free cash flow burn of $14bn.
Compute deployment is the largest swing factor for 2027 forecasts. Management targets over 2 GW exiting 4Q26 and 5-10 GW exiting 2027. DB models about 6 GW, the low end of that range.

DB has line of sight to 5-7 GW of power over the next couple of years, from Doosan Enerbility turbines, the Southaven plant, the APR acquisition, the Stateline JV (Solaris) lease, the TVA grid plant, Colossus 1 backup turbines and up to 1 GW from other sources.
DB estimates the neocloud business can generate $70-90bn of revenue in 2027, depending on timing and pricing.
DB raises 2027 revenue/EBITDA to $125bn/$84bn from $115bn/$78bn, well above consensus of $108bn/$65bn, on more than $200bn of capex. 2026 EPS falls to $0.93 from $1.06.
Investors worry that compute pricing normalizes in 2028-29. DB assumes $/GW pricing falls 25% to about $30bn in 2028.

The stock has increasingly traded in line with the AI cohort rather than Space. DB's view is that the endgame is the most compute at the lowest cost, on the ground and eventually in orbit, which investors are still skeptical about.

Other focus areas: neocloud pricing and new contracts, Cursor contribution, Grok Bot adoption, data center capex outlook, timing of the next Starship launches (Flight 15 mid/late November, no second-stage catch expected), Connectivity build-vs-buy after the Grain $8bn spectrum deal, and Tesla merger timing.

market_movers.rationale: Near-term compute demand and pricing should raise 2027 estimates, though 2028 and later is uncertain. Price was $146.03 on 16 Oct 2026.

sector_views.rationale: DB rates SpaceX Buy on its compute buildout and expects leading inference capability over time.

earnings_insights: SpaceX 3Q26 report is due tomorrow (10/20) after market close. DB estimate (not yet reported): revenue $12,633m vs consensus $12,890m, +127% YoY.
3Q26 DB estimate: GAAP gross profit $7,427m vs consensus $7,605m, gross margin 58.8% vs consensus 59.0%.
3Q26 DB estimate: adjusted EBITDA $6,640m vs consensus $6,620m. Operating income $2,031m vs consensus $2,258m.
3Q26 DB estimate: capex $18,851m vs consensus $19,610m. Free cash flow -$13,507m vs consensus -$11,600m.
3Q26 DB estimate: AI revenue $6,385m (+684% YoY) vs 2Q26 actual $2,561m. Connectivity revenue $4,943m. Space revenue $1,305m.
3Q26 DB KPI estimates vs consensus: external launches 12 vs 13, consumer broadband subs 13.5m vs 14.2m, ARPU $64 vs $65, ending compute 1.80 GW vs 1.74 GW.

DB estimate changes (non-GAAP EPS): 2026E $0.93 (from $1.06), 2027E $3.68 (from $3.44), 2028E $5.57 (from $5.62). Revenue: 2026E $46,192m, 2027E $125,250m, 2028E $200,030m. Consensus for 2027 is $108bn revenue and $65bn EBITDA.
risk_factors: Uncertainty on 2028 and beyond, with investor concern that compute pricing normalizes in 2028-29.
The stock trades more with the AI cohort than with Space, so it is exposed to AI sentiment.
Heavy capex (over $200bn in 2027E) and free cash flow burn of about $14bn in 3Q26E.
Execution on compute deployment and power procurement. The Doosan turbine order may not be SpaceX's, with unclear customer on 7 further units.
Skepticism among investors about SpaceX's inference capabilities.
geopolitical: DB says Tesla merger timing depends on valuation differentials and politics, and the company may want to avoid a potential Democrat-led administration taking over after Trump.
